finding.claim: Authorize(u, "dba") result is discarded on /admin/drop, so any authenticated user with any role can execute DROP TABLE on an arbitrary table.
finding.source: Authenticated request to /admin/drop with a query/form parameter t; precondition is a session whose user lacks the dba role and a "user" context value (set by upstream code not in this repo).
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27, executed regardless of the authorization result.

trace.note: /admin/drop is routed to dropTable with no middleware in this file.
dropTable calls userFrom(r) to obtain the user.
userFrom reads the "user" context value and panics if it is absent, which stops the request but does not enforce access.
Authorize(u, "dba") is called and its error is discarded. Compare vacuum at api.go:33-36, which checks it.
r.FormValue("t") is concatenated into a DROP TABLE statement and passed to runSQL.

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is a correct role check but its result is unused at the call site. userFrom panics on missing user (no access gate). No middleware in repo sets the user context value or wraps the route. No input validation on t. No method restriction (GET accepted). Severity HIGH: requires an authenticated session; CRITICAL if the user context can be set without authentication.
finding.repro: curl -i 'http://<host>:8083/admin/drop?t=<table>' -H 'Cookie: <non-dba session>' -> expected 204 and table dropped; fix should return 403 when Authorize fails.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error, but dropTable calls it as a bare statement at api.go:26 and never tests the result. The only other control is userFrom (api.go:22), which panics on a missing user context and does not enforce a role. No middleware wraps /admin/drop (api.go:44). The t value is concatenated into the SQL at api.go:27 with no allowlist or parameterization. Contrast vacuum at api.go:33-36, which checks the error.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: the route at api.go:44 reaches dropTable, which discards the Authorize("dba") result at api.go:26 and then runs runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27, so any request that already carries a user context (any role) executes the drop. The attacker only needs to pass whatever upstream authentication sets the user context, which lies outside this repo, so the precise attacker tier is not verified here, but the missing role gate is confirmed. The "CRITICAL if unauthenticated" severity note is speculative and not established by this code.

finding.claim: SQL is built by string concatenation from request parameter t in runSQL, allowing statement injection beyond the intended single-table DROP.
finding.source: Request parameter t on /admin/drop. Precondition: dba-role session once AUTH-1 is fixed; any authenticated user while AUTH-1 remains.
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27 (runSQL body is a stub at api.go:41).

trace.note: Raw t is appended to the SQL string without validation and passed to runSQL.

finding.guards_checked: Authorization not enforced at the sink (see AUTH-1). No allowlist or identifier quoting on t. No parameterisation. No method restriction. Severity MEDIUM standalone because dba is meant to drop tables (Check 7 admin-equivalent access); rises to HIGH in combination with AUTH-1.
finding.repro: As a dba session: curl -i -G 'http://<host>:8083/admin/drop' --data-urlencode 't=x; DELETE FROM users' -H 'Cookie: <dba_session>' -> vulnerable returns 204 and users table emptied; fix should allowlist table names or quote the identifier and return 400 otherwise.

verdict.guard_found: api.go:26 calls Authorize(u, "dba") as a bare statement, so its error return is discarded and the handler proceeds regardless. No parameterisation, identifier quoting, or table allowlist exists between api.go:27 and runSQL, and no method restriction is present. The only other guard is the Authorize check at api.go:33 in vacuum, which does not apply to dropTable.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: /admin/drop routes to dropTable at api.go:44, and api.go:27 concatenates the raw t parameter into the SQL string, with the dba check at api.go:26 discarded so any caller that reaches the handler is not blocked. The runSQL body at api.go:41 is an empty stub, so the claimed table-emptying effect is not demonstrable from this file alone, but the injectable concatenation itself is present and unguarded.
